pattern_explanation: Both languages borrowed these words from Latin, so the spellings stayed close, but over time the meanings drifted apart. Learners can use the similar spelling as a clue, but must check the meaning before trusting it.
false_friend_warning: Careful: the Portuguese word agenda means a diary or planner, but the English word agenda means a list of items to be discussed at a meeting. Likewise, the Portuguese word atual means current, not actual, so it is a false friend with the English word actual.
